chunks: My father, may Allah have mercy on him, narrated to us, saying: Ahmad ibn Idris narrated to us, from Muhammad ibn Ahmad, who said: Umar ibn Ali ibn Umar ibn Yazid narrated to me, from al-Husayn ibn Qarin, who ascribed it to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him):
He said: Indeed, the interpretation of your saying 'Ameen' is 'My Lord, do'. And it has been narrated in another hadith that 'Ameen' is a Name from the Names of Allah, Exalted and Glorious is He.

key_terms.اسْمٌ مِنْ أَسْمَاءِ اللَّهِ: a Name from the Names of Allah

ai.seo_question: What is the meaning and significance of saying 'Ameen' in Shia supplications?
ai.summary: Shaykh al-Saduq records this narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS), establishing 'Ameen' as both a supplicatory imperative meaning 'O God, accept' and a proper name of Allah, reflecting the Shia tradition of deriving liturgical terms from divine attributes. This dual interpretation underscores the theological depth of concluding prayers, linking human petition directly to the divine essence. Such linguistic precision highlights the scholarly emphasis on the spiritual efficacy of specific words in Shia jurisprudence and theology.
